_note: Invented pages and stories on reserved example domains, served by the world service only in e2e runs (STARLING_WORLD_FIXTURES with STARLING_WORLD_OFFLINE; production refuses both). Every figure here is test data, not a fact.

https://research.example.org/inference-p.title: Inference Price Index 2026: prices per token fell, spend per task did not
https://research.example.org/inference-p.text:
Across the 14 hosted models the index tracks, the median price per million output tokens fell 38% between January and September 2026.

Over the same period the median spend per completed agent task rose 12%, because the tasks used about 1.8 times as many tokens: longer contexts, more tool calls and more retries.

The index's authors say teams comparing providers should compare the cost of a finished task, not the price of a token.

https://research.example.org/saas-pricin.title: What 400 B2B SaaS pricing pages have in common
https://research.example.org/saas-pricin.text:
The study reviewed 400 pricing pages of B2B SaaS companies in August 2026.

61% offered a free trial and 23% a free plan. Pages with three tiers converted trial sign-ups 17% better than pages with five or more tiers.

Only 9% said on the page what happens when a customer outgrows their tier, and those pages had the lowest share of support questions about billing.

https://research.example.org/protein-tim.title: Review: total daily protein matters more than timing for muscle growth
https://research.example.org/protein-tim.text:
The review pooled 32 trials of adults doing resistance training.

Total daily protein, about 1.6 g per kg of body weight, explained most of the difference in muscle gain between groups. Spreading it over three or four meals added a small benefit; the timing of a single post-workout shake made no measurable difference.

The authors conclude that for most people the practical advice is to hit a daily total first and worry about timing last.

news.title: Open-weight model matches hosted rivals on a public evals suite at a fraction of the inference cost
news.summary: An open-weight model scored within two points of the leading hosted models on a public evals suite while costing about a tenth as much to serve, according to its developers.

news.title: Survey: retries and tool calls, not the model, drive most LLM latency in production
news.summary: A survey of 300 teams running LLM apps found that retries and tool calls account for most of their p95 latency; model inference itself was the largest share for fewer than a third.

news.title: Cloud provider cuts batch inference prices for ML infrastructure teams
news.summary: A large cloud provider cut prices for batch inference jobs by 30% this week, aimed at ML infrastructure teams running evals and offline workloads.

news.title: Bootstrapped SaaS founders who raised prices this year saw churn hold steady, survey finds
news.summary: A survey of 250 bootstrapped B2B SaaS founders found that most who raised prices in 2026 saw no rise in churn; the most common regret was waiting too long.

news.title: Support-led growth: small SaaS companies turn support tickets into their roadmap
news.summary: Several profitable small SaaS businesses describe reading every support ticket as their main source of product research, and cutting churn by fixing what the tickets name.

news.title: Payments provider adds simpler annual plans for small business subscriptions
news.summary: A payments provider launched a simpler way for small businesses to offer annual plans, citing lower churn for annual customers.

news.title: New review busts the meal-frequency myth: total protein beats eating every three hours
news.summary: A review of nutrition trials found no metabolic benefit from eating every three hours; total daily protein and calories mattered far more, a finding that busts a long-running fitness myth.

news.title: Strength training twice a week linked to longer life in large study
news.summary: Adults who did strength training at least twice a week had lower mortality over ten years than those who did none, in a large observational study; the benefit held for beginners who started late.

news.title: Walking counts: daily steps study backs practical training advice for busy people
news.summary: A study of daily step counts found health benefits levelling off around 7,000 steps a day, supporting practical nutrition advice and training plans built around walking for busy people.
